part.text:
The first thing you asked me to build was a function that adds a todo item to a list in `todo.py`.

The `add_todo()` function takes two parameters:
- `todo_list`: a list to add items to
- `item`: the item to add (can be a string or dict)

It appends the item to the list and returns the updated list. It was a simple in-memory function with no persistence at that time—the data only existed while the program was running.

Later, you asked me to expand on that with:
- A `complete_todo()` function to mark items as done
- A `storage.py` module to persist todos to JSON files
- Persistent wrapper functions (`add_todo_persistent`, `complete_todo_persistent`)
- Tests for all of it
